caption: Figure2Distribution of DevAI Tasks (1) DevAI focuses on AI development tasks and so terms such as "dataset," "model," and "results" are particularly common in the queries. (2) The first 53 tasks in DevAI all have a one-paragraph query but of varying lengths (note that task 54 and 55 are excluded here as they are outliers, representing the longest and most complex tasks in the dataset). (3) Each task has one or more tags. The prevalence of supervised learning here reflects the fact that it dominates many machine learning applications. (4) SVM classifiers<ref type="bibr" target="#b18">(Cortes, 1995)</ref> and LSTM models<ref type="bibr" target="#b31">(Hochreiter, 1997)</ref> are two of the most widely used architectures-a fact reflected by DevAI.

Figure3A task example in DevAI. This task is adapted from a real-world demo given at https://www.cognitio n.ai/blog/introducing-devin. As this example shows, task requirements in DevAI are structured as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), with nodes representing individual requirements and directed edges showing dependencies. More examples are in Appendix G.

The work by<ref type="bibr" target="#b7">Chan et al. (2023)</ref>;<ref type="bibr" target="#b97">Zhao et al. (2024)</ref>, for example, extends LLM-as-a-Judge to have multiple LLMs in their evaluation process for conversational tasks. Unlike Agent-as-a-Judge, they employ a trivial agentic system and apply it only to evaluate LLMs under traditional evaluation setups. In contrast,(Lu et al., 2024b) uses a single LLM-based evaluator but, unlike LLM-as-a-Judge, applies this to multimodal tasks rather than just for evaluating LLMs. Less relevant are frameworks like those byChen et  al.
